subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should OpenClaw accept the current allowlist/config-based fix candidate for shared-workspace Dreaming isolation, or require a narrower agent-boundary fix before this issue can close?
rationale: The bug is security-relevant and current docs favor isolated agents, but the open fix candidate adds public plugin config and SDK surface that needs maintainer acceptance before it becomes the durable boundary.

options.title: Review And Land Or Replace The Fix Candidate
options.body: Resolve the current PR's merge blockers and security/config review, then close this issue only after a reviewed agent-scoped Dreaming fix lands.

options.title: Require A Narrower Isolation-Only Fix
options.body: Reject the public config/API direction and ask for a smaller patch that enforces per-agent Dreaming isolation without adding new operator surface.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling As Expected
options.body: Treat shared-workspace Dreaming pooling as intentional and document it, accepting the privacy and identity-contamination tradeoff reported here.

recommendation.title: Review And Land Or Replace The Fix Candidate
recommendation.body: Resolve the current PR's merge blockers and security/config review, then close this issue only after a reviewed agent-scoped Dreaming fix lands.

likelyOwner.reason: This issue is assigned to vincentkoc, and their existing comments already framed the unresolved shared-workspace isolation decision.
